3D reference lines

Source: R/geom-refline-3d.R
geom_refline_3d.Rd

geom_refline_3d() draws infinite straight lines, clipped to the panel, such as the line spanned by a vector, or a vertical reference line. Each line passes through the point x, y, z in the direction dx, dy, dz.

Usage

geom_refline_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  x = 0,
  y = 0,
  z = 0,
  dx,
  dy,
  dz,
  scale_depth = TRUE,
  on_top = FALSE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by aes(), mapping the direction components dx, dy, and dz. Used only when no direction is given as a parameter.

data

The data to be displayed in this layer.

...

Other arguments passed on to layer(), such as aesthetics like colour, linewidth, linetype, and alpha.

x, y, z

Coordinates of the point each line passes through. Default 0.

dx, dy, dz

Components of each line's direction. Each defaults to 0, but they can't all be zero.

scale_depth

Controls depth-based scaling, drawing closer elements larger or thicker and farther ones smaller or thinner. TRUE (the default) applies full scaling and FALSE disables it; a number sets the strength directly, where 1 matches TRUE, 0 matches FALSE, values below 1 subdue the effect and values above 1 exaggerate it. This affects the layer only; use coord_3d(scale_depth = ) for panel and axis components.

on_top

If TRUE, the layer is drawn on top of the rest of the scene instead of being depth-sorted with it, so other geometry never hides or cuts it, e.g. to keep labels legible. The layers drawn on top are depth-sorted among themselves. Default FALSE.

na.rm

If FALSE, lines with missing directions are removed with a warning.

show.legend

Logical indicating whether this layer should be included in legends. Lines given as parameters are never included.

inherit.aes

If TRUE, combine the plot's default aesthetics with mapping. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Directions can be given as parameters, as vectors to draw several lines, or mapped from data in aes(). The point a line passes through is always a parameter, since it would otherwise affect the axes' ranges; when lines are given as parameters, it can be a vector giving each line's point, and when directions are mapped, it is a single point shared by all lines.

Lines are built from the panel's limits when the plot is drawn, so they don't expand the plot's axis ranges; a line that misses the panel entirely is skipped with a warning. They are depth-sorted with the rest of the scene, and drawn on top of any plane or polygon they lie in. Positions and directions are in the plot's (transformed) scale space.

Aesthetics

geom_refline_3d() understands the following aesthetics: dx, dy, dz, colour, linewidth, linetype, and alpha.

Examples

# The line spanned by a vector, and a vertical line at x = 1, y = 2
v <- c(2, 1, 1.5)
ggplot(data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, xend = v[1], yend = v[2], zend = v[3]),
       aes(x, y, z, xend = xend, yend = yend, zend = zend)) +
  geom_segment_3d(arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(8, "pt"))) +
  geom_refline_3d(dx = v[1], dy = v[2], dz = v[3], linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_refline_3d(x = 1, y = 2, dz = 1, colour = "red") +
  lims(x = c(-1, 3), y = c(-1, 3)) + zlim(-1, 3) +
  coord_3d()


# The line along which two planes intersect
ggplot() +
  geom_plane_3d(a = c(1, 1), b = c(1, -1), c = c(1, 0), d = c(1, 0),
                fill = c("tomato", "steelblue")) +
  geom_refline_3d(x = 0.5, y = 0.5, z = 0, dx = 1, dy = 1, dz = -2,
                  linewidth = 1) +
  lims(x = c(-1, 1), y = c(-1, 1)) + zlim(-1, 1) +
  coord_3d()
